headline: Sustainability is using resources at a rate they can regenerate—taking only what replenishes
universal_truth: You can't draw from a well forever if you take more than it refills; match consumption to regeneration
fun_facts: Earth Overshoot Day—when humanity has used a year's worth of resources—falls earlier each year
Sustainable fishing quotas allow fish populations to recover; overfishing has collapsed many fisheries
Bamboo is considered sustainable because it grows up to 35 inches per day
discussion_questions: What resources are you consuming faster than they regenerate?
Where do you need to reduce consumption or increase regeneration?
What sustainable practices have you adopted?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Imagine a bank account where you spend more than you earn. Eventually, you're broke. Now imagine that with forests, fisheries, energy, even your own health. Sustainability is matching withdrawal to deposit—taking only what replenishes.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Unsustainable practices seem fine—until they're not. The crash comes when resources are exhausted. How do we live sustainably?

options.text: Sustainable living requires tracking resources, consuming at or below regeneration rates, and actively investing in renewal—not just taking less, but ensuring replenishment
options.response: Yes. Sustainability needs both sides: reduce consumption AND support regeneration. It's not just taking less—it's ensuring what you take can be replaced.
Using less helps, but true sustainability also requires regeneration...

q1.title: Regeneration Rates
q1.script: Every resource has a regeneration rate. Forests regrow at certain speeds. Energy can be renewed. Even personal energy replenishes. Sustainability means matching consumption to regeneration.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Regeneration Rates"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Delayed Consequences
q2.script: Unsustainable practices don't fail immediately—consequences lag. This makes it easy to ignore them. By the time problems are obvious, damage is done. Sustainability requires thinking ahead.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Sustainability
q3.script: Your energy, health, and relationships are resources too. Burnout is unsustainability—consuming faster than regenerating. Recovery time matters. Sustainable living applies to you, not just the planet.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You can't draw from a well forever if you take more than it refills. Match consumption to regeneration—in resources and in life.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 236. Tomorrow, we'll explore weather patterns over time—climate. Until then, audit one resource for sustainability.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Sustainability Check - Consumption vs Regeneration
growTrack.activity: Pick a resource you depend on: energy, time, money, relationships, health. Are you consuming faster than it regenerates? What would sustainable look like? Sometimes small reductions in consumption, combined with investment in regeneration, transform unsustainable patterns.
